The user wants to list all current files in the temp directory, including hidden files, without changing the current directory structure or generating any extra directories or files. So we need to run ls -a in the temp directory. We should use the ls function with a=True. But we need to ensure we are in the temp directory. We might need to cd into temp first. But the user says "in temp directory" so we should cd into temp. But they also say "ensure we keep the current directory structure unchanged". That means we shouldn't create any new directories or files. Changing directory is fine. So we can cd into temp, then ls -a. Then maybe return to previous directory? But the user didn't ask to return. They just want to list. So we can cd into temp, then ls -a. Let's do that.

We need to call cd with folder="temp". Then ls with a=True.
